walkthroughs.body_html:
How much of a compound is one element?

% of element = (Ar × number of atoms) ÷ Mr × 100

Example: % of O in H₂O = 16 ÷ 18 × 100 = 88.9%.

Reactions rarely give 100% — some product is lost, or the reaction doesn't go fully.

% yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100

If theory says 20 g but you get 15 g, % yield = 15 ÷ 20 × 100 = 75%.

Atom economy measures how much of your reactant mass ends up as useful product.

% atom economy = (Mr of useful product ÷ total Mr of reactants) × 100

High atom economy = less waste = greener chemistry.

mcqs.q: Theoretical yield is 50 g, actual yield is 40 g. What is the % yield?
Why do industries care about atom economy?
options: Higher atom economy means less waste and more sustainability
It makes reactions faster
It increases the boiling point
It changes the colour of products

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
